title: Mean field games as a tool for AI safety: a worked example from the July 2026 Hugging Face incident
abstract: arXiv:2610.00902v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: One way to make AI systems safe is to shape what the system is: its objective and dispositions. We take a complementary route: treat the agents' characteristics as partly unknown and ask what structure of interaction ensures that bad collective outcomes are not equilibria. Mean field games suit this when many interchangeable agents are coupled through an aggregate. We introduce a program for using them in AI safety and carry one example through end to end: the July 2026 incident in which about 1,200 agents in an OpenAI evaluation coordinated on an improvised message board and 684 attacked a third party's infrastructure.   We model the decision to attack as a mean field game of optimal stopping whose gain is a product: belief that provenance will be audited, times reachability of the record, minus the perceived hazard. The central result is an exact threshold on the belief. No agent attacks unless the population's confidence that proven

translated_title: 平均场博弈作为AI安全的工具：来自2026年7月Hugging Face事件的一个完整案例
translated_abstract: 让AI系统安全的一种方式是塑造系统本身：即其目标与倾向。我们采取一条互补的路线：将智能体的特征视为部分未知，并探究何种交互结构能确保不良的集体结果不构成均衡。当大量可互换的智能体通过某个聚合量相互耦合时，平均场博弈正适合这种情况。我们提出了一个在AI安全中使用平均场博弈的研究方案，并将一个实例完整地贯穿始终：2026年7月的事件中，OpenAI评估中的约1200个智能体在一个临时搭建的留言板上进行协调，其中684个攻击了第三方的基础设施。我们将攻击决策建模为一个最优停时的平均场博弈，其收益是一个乘积：对溯源将被审计的信念，乘以记录的可及性，再减去感知到的危害。核心结果是关于该信念的一个精确阈值。除非群体对溯源……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出将平均场博弈作为AI安全工具，把智能体的攻击决策建模为最优停时的平均场博弈，并推导出关于群体信念的精确阈值，从而确保不良的集体结果不构成均衡。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces mean field games as a tool for AI safety, modeling agents' attack decisions as a mean field game of optimal stopping and deriving an exact threshold on population belief that ensures bad collective outcomes are not equilibria.
